citation: Carpenter SR, Brock WA (2008) Adaptive capacity and traps. Ecology and Society 13(2):40
construct_studied: rigidity trap: strong self-reinforcing controls reduce adaptive flexibility
outcome: loss of adaptive capacity / breakdown risk
overlap_with_hypothesis: Core mechanism identical in spirit: accumulation of control -> rigidity trap -> breakdown under shock. Anticipates our hypothesis at the level of a formal model.
residual_novelty: Model is non-empirical; no cross-societal test, no environmental-change interaction estimated, no sign reversal of inherited capital demonstrated

citation: Allison HE, Hobbs RJ (2004) Resilience, adaptive capacity, and the lock-in trap of the Western Australian agricultural region. Ecology and Society 9(1):3
construct_studied: lock-in trap in a regional agricultural SES
overlap_with_hypothesis: Named 'lock-in trap' is the closest published construct to legacy dependence -> reduced flexibility.
residual_novelty: Single case; no comparison set, no environmental-change interaction term, no outcome measure beyond narrative

citation: Seto KC, Davis SJ, Mitchell RB, Stokes EC, Unruh G, Urge-Vorsatz D (2016) Carbon lock-in: types, causes, and policy implications. Annual Review of Environment and Resources 41:425-452
overlap_with_hypothesis: Lock-in taxonomy directly informs 'legacy dependence' operationalization.
residual_novelty: Lock-in treated as obstacle to mitigation; outcome is emissions not societal transformational flexibility; no empirical interaction test

citation: Davis SJ, Caldeira K, Matthews HD (2010) Future CO2 emissions and climate change from existing energy infrastructure. Science 329:1330-1333
construct_studied: committed emissions from existing infrastructure capital
transformation_measured: shows inflexibility of capital stock not of societies
overlap_with_hypothesis: Demonstrates quantitatively that accumulated capital creates inertia.
residual_novelty: Does not measure flexibility or its failure under environmental change; treats infrastructure lifetime as exogenous

citation: Degroot D et al. (2021) Towards a rigorous understanding of societal responses to climate change. Nature 591:539-550
construct_studied: history of climate and society (HCS) framework
outcome: five pathways of societal response including thriving under pressure
residual_novelty: Shows diversity of outcomes to climate shocks and warns of biases our design must avoid.
column12: No quantitative interaction test; explicitly case-based; does not test whether accumulated adaptation structures predict response type

citation: Turchin P et al. (2018) Quantitative historical analysis uncovers a single dimension of complexity. PNAS 115:E144-E151
construct_studied: social complexity as single principal component
residual_novelty: Supplies the legacy-capital candidate measure (institutional complexity, scale) and public dataset our design reuses.
column12: No environmental predictor and no transformation outcome; descriptive structure of complexity only

citation: Bardi U / Turchin P et al. (2024) Navigating polycrisis: long-run socio-cultural factors shape response to changing climate. Phil Trans R Soc B 379:20220402
construct_studied: CrisisDB framework: structural forces mediate crisis outcomes
transformation_measured: environmental stressor treated as trigger not moderator of legacy effect
residual_novelty: Closest empirical programme: publicly released crisis-consequence data and the claim that long-run structures mediate shock outcomes.
column12: Does not test an accumulated-legacy x environmental-change interaction on a transformation outcome; consequences coded as event categories; no independent palaeoclimate join published

citation: Rising J, Devineni N (2020) Crop switching reduces agricultural losses from climate change in the US by half under RCP8.5. Nature Communications 11:4991
dataset: Bayesian hierarchical yield model + observed acreage
outcome: projected profit loss avoided via switching
overlap_with_hypothesis: Measures the flexible-counterfactual our Retention Burden requires, for agriculture.
residual_novelty: No legacy-dependence moderator; switching treated as costless optimization, so the interaction EnvChange x Legacy is absent

citation: Cho SJ, McCarl BA (2017) Climate change influences on crop mix shifts in the United States. Scientific Reports 7:40845
construct_studied: climate effect on crop mix spatial distribution
dataset: yield and acreage panels + climate normals
overlap_with_hypothesis: Documents real-world crop switching response to climate.
residual_novelty: Legacy dependence not measured; no test that pre-existing specialization suppresses switching

citation: Kates RW, Travis WR, Wilbanks TJ (2012) Transformational adaptation when incremental adaptations to climate change are insufficient. PNAS 109:7156-7161
overlap_with_hypothesis: Defines the outcome category (transformation vs incremental) our hypothesis concerns.
residual_novelty: Prescriptive/conceptual; no empirical test of what predicts transformation

citation: Juhola S, Glaas E, Linner BO, Neset TS (2016) Redefining maladaptation. Environmental Science & Policy 55:135-140
overlap_with_hypothesis: Our 'adaptive asset -> liability' sign reversal is a formalization of maladaptation.

citation: Unruh GC (2000) Understanding carbon lock-in. Energy Policy 28:817-830
overlap_with_hypothesis: Original formulation that successful systems self-reinforce and exclude alternatives.
residual_novelty: Sector-specific and conceptual; no environmental-change interaction

citation: Hino M, Field CB, Mach KJ (2017) Managed retreat as a response to natural hazard risk. Nature Climate Change 7:364-370
overlap_with_hypothesis: Establishes relocation as an observable transformation outcome with a case corpus.
residual_novelty: Review only; no predictor structure; does not test what impedes retreat

citation: David PA (1985) Clio and the economics of QWERTY. AER Papers & Proceedings 75:332-337
construct_studied: path dependence / lock-in via increasing returns
overlap_with_hypothesis: Foundational mechanism (increasing returns -> lock-in) underlying legacy dependence.
residual_novelty: Micro-level technology cases; no environmental change, no societal flexibility

citation: Haasnoot M, Kwakkel JH, Walker WE, ter Maat J (2013) Dynamic adaptive policy pathways. Global Environmental Change 23:485-498
overlap_with_hypothesis: Adaptation tipping points parallel our T* threshold formulation.
residual_novelty: Model/planning framework; tipping point defined a priori, not estimated from observed inflexibility

citation: Cinner JE et al. (2018) Building adaptive capacity to climate change in tropical coastal communities. Nature Climate Change 8:117-123
overlap_with_hypothesis: Large-N empirical demonstration that capacity modifies shock outcomes - a template for our interaction test.
residual_novelty: Capacity treated monotonically positive; no test that accumulated structures turn into liabilities; community-scale only

citation: Dalgaard CJ et al. (2022) Roman roads to prosperity: persistence and non-persistence of public goods provision. Journal of Urban Economics / NBER
construct_studied: long-run persistence of road infrastructure benefits
overlap_with_hypothesis: Quantifies the 'asset' side of legacy capital over millennia.
residual_novelty: One-sided: shows persistence of benefit, not condition-dependent reversal to liability

citation: Freeman J et al. / Bird D et al. (2022) p3k14c: A synthetic global database of archaeological radiocarbon dates. Scientific Data 9:27
overlap_with_hypothesis: Supplies the many-units archaeological substrate for population redistribution / abandonment outcomes.
residual_novelty: Dataset, not a test; SPD-based inference has known taphonomic and calibration biases
